newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP says steel output to fall in Feb.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP says steel output to fall in Feb.

text.p: Australia's biggest raw steel maker, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, said on Tuesday that steel production fell slightly in January and production from its Port Kembla plant would fall in February as a blast furnace was brought back to full output.
BHP's raw steel production fell two percent to 696,000 tonnes in January from January a year earlier, while steel despatches fell two percent to 643,000 tonnes from January 1996.
"Lower Port Kembla steelmaker for January was due to a breakout of molten iron at No 5 blast furnace on January 17 resulting in a two week shutdown," BHP said.
"Steel production at Port Kembla is expected to be lower during February as the blast furnace is brought back to full production," BHP said.
Steel production fell at BHP's Sydney Steel Mill because the annual maintenance shutdown extended six days into January.
"Despatches from overseas operations increased 24 percent in January reflecting new capacity in Malaysia and Singapore and increased production from Indonesia and the United States."

Raw steelmake production fell three percent to 5.598 million tonnes in the eight months to January from the corresponding eight months a year earlier. Total steel despatches rose four percent to 5.399 million in the eight months.
BHP's domestic steel despatches rose to 334,000 tonnes in January from 327,000 tonnes in January 1996, while BHP Australia's export despatches fell to 222,000 tonnes from 248,000 a year earlier.
Despatches of flat steel products rose to 463,000 tonnes in January from 395,000 tonnes a year earlier, while long products fell to 207,000 tonnes from 251,000 tonnes.
